title: The Promise of an Eternal King

sections.title: Look Back (Review)
paragraphs: Pray for one another.
Read

God said to Samuel, “The people have again rejected me as their King. Give the people what they are asking for but warn them that “the king will take your sons and daughters and make them work for him. He will take the best from the land. When that happens, you will cry out for relief from your king, but I will not answer you.” But the people still demanded a king.

sections.title: Look Up (New Teaching)
paragraphs: Read

God told Samuel to anoint Israel’s first king (King Saul). At first, Saul was a good king. He led the people to many great victories. One day Saul became impatient with God. Samuel had told Saul to wait for him to give the sacrifice to the Lord, but Saul gave the sacrifice himself. When Samuel arrived, he told Saul, “You did not obey the command of the Lord; therefore, God has rejected you as king. God has found a person who follows after His own heart, because to obey is better than sacrifice.”
God sent Samuel to anoint another man, David, as king. David was called a man after God’s own heart. David was not perfect, but he did lead God’s people along the right path.
Read
Let’s read some verses from the Holy Scriptures, the Bible, that relate to this story.
1 Samuel 16:1–13
2 Samuel 7:1–17
Read

These verses teach us that God's grace keeps its promise, even to flawed people. David also sinned, yet God did not abandon him. God kept His covenant with David and promised that from his descendants an eternal king would come. God's grace did not wait for David to become worthy. It held him through his failure and carried the promise forward. God’s promise was fulfilled in Jesus Christ, the king from David's line, who will reign forever with grace and truth.
Ask
What did you learn from these Scriptures?
Think a little — how will you practice what you have learned?

sections.title: Look Forward (Obedience)
paragraphs: Do
Have you ever been disappointed when someone didn’t keep their promise? Let’s thank God that he always keeps his word.
Ask
I hope you enjoyed this story. When can we meet again?
Do you think someone else should hear this story?
